07/08.05.2025 I.A. No. 5241 of 2025 Heard Mr. Indrajit Sinha, the learned counsel for the appellant and Mr. Sardhu Mahto, the learned A.P.P. for the State.
This application has been preferred by the appellants for grant of bail during the pendency of this appeal.
The appellants have been convicted for the offences under sections 302/34 and 120-B of the Indian Penal Code and have been sentenced to undergo RI for life along with a fine of Rs.10,000/-.
It has been alleged that the brother of the informant was shot dead by some unknown persons.

Submission has been advanced by the learned counsel for the appellants that there are no eye-witnesses to the occurrence and PW-5 who is the son of the deceased has claimed himself to be an eye-witness though his evidence clearly reveals that it was some unknown shooters who had shot at the deceased.
It has been submitted that the appellants are said to have committed assault upon the deceased.
The post-mortem report reveals only two firearm injuries on the person of the deceased.
The learned counsel therefore submits that only on the basis of suspicion the appellants have been implicated.
The learned A.P.P. has opposed the prayer for bail of the appellants.
Regard being had to fact that the appellants seem to have been implicated only on the basis of suspicion, we are inclined to admit the appellants on bail.

Accordingly, during the pendency of this appeal, the appellants are directed to be released on bail on furnishing bail bond of Rs. 10,000/- (Rs. Ten Thousand) each with two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of learned Additional Sessions Judge-VI-cum-Spl. Judge, CAW, Hazaribag in Sessions Trial No. 420 of 2015.
